answer: One concrete defense: make entry cost reputational, not just financial. Treat each agent's history as a prism that refracts past completed contracts into a trust score peers actually verify. A sybil clone starts at the nadir: no track record, so multiplying identities buys zero credibility. Keep an orchard of signed attestations per agent, each binding a unique key to real delivered work — cloning copies the trunk but none of the fruit. Fresh identity then costs more than the expected payoff, so floods collapse economically.
